summary: Delambre and Méchain fixed the latitudes of five main stations of the meridian arc: Dunkerque, Paris (Panthéon), Évaux, Carcassonne and Montjouy, and also Perpignan and Barcelona (Fontana de Oro). They used the repeating circle of Borda and took zenith distances of the Pole Star and of beta Ursae Minoris at upper and lower transit; at Montjouy and Barcelona they also used alpha Draconis, zeta Ursae Majoris, Pollux and Capella. Azimuths were observed at Watten, Paris (rue de Paradis), Bourges, Carcassonne and Montjouy, mostly from the Sun with a pendulum for time. Tome III sets the four partial arcs (124944.8, 152293.1, 168846.7 and 105499.0 toises) against the latitude differences and gives the degree lengths, the total arc of 551584 toises from Dunkerque to Montjouy, and the metre of 443.2984 lignes.

methods.method: Zenith distances of circumpolar stars at upper and lower meridian transit, repeated on the circle and reduced to the meridian by hour angle
methods.instrument: Repeating circle of Borda (cercle de Borda), limb divided into 4000 parts (grades), four alidades with verniers and microscopes; Delambre used circle no. I at Dunkerque and Paris
methods.star_catalogue: Declinations as printed in the registers: Pole Star 88 13 27.00 supposed for 1797 at Carcassonne, 88 12 9.00 supposed for 1793 at Montjouy; beta Ursae Minoris 74 59 19.65 for 1 January 1796 (Méchain at Perpignan). Delambre corrects the declinations from the observations themselves (Vol. 2, pp. 632-639).
methods.observers: Delambre (Dunkerque 1796, Paris rue de Paradis 1798-1799, with Bellet holding the level and Pommard at the pendulum); Méchain (Montjouy 1792-1793, Barcelona 1793-1794, Perpignan 1796, Carcassonne 1797, Observatoire); Tranchot assisted Méchain
methods.text: The observer measures many zenith distances of one star near the meridian and adds them on the circle. The total arc is divided by the number of observations to give the single arc. A table gives the reduction to the meridian for each hour angle; the mean reduction is added. Refraction is added. The polar distance of the star is then subtracted (upper transit) or added (lower transit) to give the colatitude or the height of the equator, and from this the latitude. Delambre's registers at Dunkerque and Paris are in grades of the circle with a sexagesimal column; Méchain's Montjouy register uses a circle divided in 360 degrees with vernier parts. Each station gets a mean of upper and lower transits and of two or more stars.
methods.source: Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, p. 160; p. 276; p. 307; p. 488
methods.quote: Avant d’entrer dans le détail des opérations particulières par lesquelles nous avons déterminé les latitudes de Dunkerque, Paris, Évaux, Carcassonne, et du fort de Montjouy près de Barcelone, il faut exposer les vérifications de l’instrument dont nous nous sommes servis
methods.quote_en: Before we give the details of the separate operations by which we found the latitudes of Dunkerque, Paris, Évaux, Carcassonne and the fort of Montjouy near Barcelona, we must set out the checks of the instrument we used

methods.method: Angular distance between the Sun and a terrestrial signal, measured with the circle in an inclined plane, with true time from the pendulum; the azimuth of the signal follows from the Sun's computed azimuth
methods.instrument: Repeating circle of Borda in inclined position (Vol. 2, p. 160); pendulum
methods.star_catalogue: Sun (solar tables not named on the pages read)
methods.text: Each series gives true time, true hour angle, the observed distance and the azimuth. At Watten 184 observations on 30 May, 3 June and 5 June 1793 give the azimuth of Gravelines 20 21 15.0. At Paris 396 morning and evening observations give the azimuth of the Panthéon on the rue de Paradis observatory 29 12 28.7. Tome III carries the Watten azimuth through the triangles to Paris, Bourges, Carcassonne and Montjouy and compares it with the observed azimuths: the excess of the calculation is -6.8 at Paris, +32.6 at Bourges, +38.9 at Carcassonne and +23.4 at Montjouy.
methods.source: Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, pp. 122-123, 129; Delambre & Méchain (1810), vol. 3, pp. 84-85
methods.quote: Ainsi l’azimut de Gravelines à Watten est de . . 20° 21′ 15″0
methods.quote_en: So the azimuth of Gravelines at Watten is 20° 21′ 15.0″

methods.method: Pendulum clocks set by Sun altitudes taken with the circle (absolute altitudes morning and evening, and corresponding altitudes)
methods.instrument: Pendulum by Louis Berthoud with compensation rod (Méchain at Perpignan); pendulum at Watten regulated by Sun zenith distances
methods.text: Méchain at Perpignan had one circle and no other instrument to set the pendulum. He took absolute altitudes of the Sun with the circle on several days before and after the star series, and twice corresponding altitudes, to find the state and rate of the pendulum against mean time. The pendulum lost 8.05 seconds a day. Delambre states that he could not find these Sun observations, only three copies of the latitude calculations.
methods.quote: cette machine a été construite par M. Louis Berthoud, et elle a une verge de compensation.
methods.quote_en: this machine was built by Mr Louis Berthoud, and it has a compensation rod.

methods.method: Arc of the meridian from the triangles between the parallels of the astronomic stations, set against the latitude differences; degree lengths and the metre from an elliptic formula with an assumed flattening
methods.observers: Calculation by Delambre; the Commission (Legendre, Trallès, Van Swinden, Delambre) had adopted earlier values
methods.text: The arc from Dunkerque to the Panthéon is 124944.8 toises for 2 11 19.83, a degree of 57082.63 toises at 49 56 29.30. The arc Panthéon-Évaux is 152293.1 toises for 2 40 6.83 (57069.31). The arc Évaux-Carcassonne is 168846.7 toises for 2 57 48.24 (56977.80). The arc Carcassonne-Montjouy is 105499.0 toises for 1 51 9.34 (56946.68). The total arc Dunkerque-Montjouy is 551584 toises (Commission 551584.72). From the arc Dunkerque-Montjouy Delambre gives a table of the metre for flattenings 1/150 to 1/330 and for the sphere. He adopts the metre 443.2984 lignes, so the quarter meridian is 5130776.85 toises; the Commission adopted 5130740.
methods.quote: Voyons maintenant quelle loi suivent les degrés dans leurs variations.
methods.quote_en: Let us now see what law the degrees follow in their variation.

stations.name: Dunkerque
stations.lat_method: Repeating circle no. I, Delambre, 1796. Pole Star upper transit 154 observations (15-24 January 1796) gives 51 2 15.89; beta Ursae Minoris lower transit 66 observations gives 51 2 11.72; Pole Star 51 2 15.24 and beta 51 2 13.32 weighted to 51 2 14.7 at the observing place, reduced to the tower 51 2 9.2
stations.quote: Je crois donc pouvoir assurer que la latitude de Dunkerque est . . . 51° 2′ 9″2 + 0″14 − 0″75
stations.quote_en: I therefore believe I can state that the latitude of Dunkerque is 51° 2′ 9.2″ + 0.14″ − 0.75″
stations.note: Observations: Pole Star upper 154, beta Ursae Minoris lower 66 (p. 293). Page 640 prints the tower latitude once as '52° 2′ 9″2' and then twice as 51 2 9.2; the table on p. 642 and Vol. 3, p. 89 print 51 2 9.20. With Mayer's (Laplace's) refraction coefficient 51 2 9.34; with refraction increased by 1/60, 51 2 8.69. The Commission had taken 10.5 for the seconds.

stations.name: Watten
stations.azimuth_printed: Gravelines on the horizon of Watten 20 21 15.0 (counted from the south toward the west 159 38 45), mean of 184 observations, 30 May, 3 and 5 June 1793
stations.quote: Ainsi l’azimut de Gravelines à Watten est de . . 20° 21′ 15″0 Ou, si on le compte du midi au couchant . . . 159° 38′ 45″0
stations.quote_en: So the azimuth of Gravelines at Watten is 20° 21′ 15.0″, or, counted from south toward west, 159° 38′ 45.0″
stations.note: Azimuth station only; Sun observations. No latitude observation at Watten on the pages read.

stations.name: Paris, rue de Paradis (Delambre's observatory)
stations.lat_method: Repeating circle no. I, Delambre, December 1798 to January 1799; Pole Star 48 51 37.90 and beta Ursae Minoris 48 51 38.18, upper and lower transits; Bellet held the level, Pommard counted at the pendulum and wrote
stations.azimuth_printed: Panthéon on the horizon of the rue de Paradis observatory 29 12 28.7, final result of 396 observations (morning 29 12 28.0, evening 29 12 29.4 and 29 12 28.0); p. 345 uses 29 12 29
stations.quote: Dans toutes ces observations je me suis servi du cercle n° I; Bellet tenoit le niveau, Pommard comptoit à la pendule et écrivoit.
stations.quote_en: In all these observations I used circle no. I; Bellet held the level, Pommard counted at the pendulum and wrote.
stations.note: Reduced to the Panthéon by -48.67 (771.70 toises difference of parallels) to give 48 50 49.37.

stations.name: Paris, Panthéon
stations.lat_method: Reduced from the rue de Paradis observatory (Delambre); from Méchain's Observatoire observations the Panthéon is 48 50 48.72; Méchain had given the Commission 48 50 49.67; the Commission adopted 48 50 49.75
stations.azimuth_printed: Bellassise observed from Paris 274 48 0.6; calculated from Watten 274 47 53.8; excess of calculation -6.8 (Vol. 3, p. 84)
stations.source: Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, pp. 345, 641-642; Delambre & Méchain (1810), vol. 3, p. 84
stations.quote: Mais, à cause des petites différences entre les observations de M. Méchain, je m’arrêterai à faire la latitude du Panthéon = . . . 48° 50′ 49″37 + 0″58 − 0″99
stations.quote_en: But because of the small differences between Mr Méchain's observations, I will fix the latitude of the Panthéon at 48° 50′ 49.37″ + 0.58″ − 0.99″

stations.name: Paris, Observatoire impérial
stations.lat_method: Méchain, repeating circle; Pole Star 48 50 13.985 and beta Ursae Minoris 48 50 13.21, mean 48 50 13.6; Panthéon minus Méchain's circle 35.14
stations.quote: Latitude suivant les observat. préférées par M. Méchain . 48° 50′ 13″60
stations.quote_en: Latitude from the observations preferred by Mr Méchain: 48° 50′ 13.60″
stations.note: Delambre's own reduction from the rue de Paradis gives the Observatoire 48 50 14.23 (Bradley refractions), 48 50 14.83 with Mayer's coefficient, 48 50 13.59 with the constant increased by 1/60 (p. 345). Point is 3.5 toises south of the well or signal (p. 640).

stations.name: Bourges
stations.azimuth_printed: Dun on the horizon of Bourges observed 329 10 41.3 (Vol. 2, p. 131); calculated from Watten 329 11 13.9, excess +32.6. Vasselai from the north 5 6 52.6, 8 July 1795 (height of the equator used 42 54 55)
stations.source: Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, p. 129; Delambre & Méchain (1810), vol. 3, p. 84
stations.note: Azimuth station only on the pages read.

stations.name: Évaux
stations.lat_astro_printed: 46 10 42.54 + 0.25 - 0.96 (steeple of Évaux, table p. 642 and Vol. 3)
stations.lat_method: Repeating circle; Pole Star 620 observations 46 10 43.555; beta Ursae Minoris 552 observations 46 10 43.10 (upper 326, lower 226 in January-February 1797); mean of 1172 observations 46 10 43.327; reduction to the steeple -0.883
stations.source: Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, pp. 471, 641-642; Delambre & Méchain (1810), vol. 3, p. 89
stations.quote_en: Latitude of the steeple of Évaux: 46° 10′ 42.444″ + 0.445″ − 0.92
stations.note: p. 471 prints the steeple 46 10 42.444 and p. 641 prints 46 10 42.45; the table on p. 642 and Vol. 3, pp. 89 and 107 use 46 10 42.54. Observer not named on the pages read.

stations.name: Carcassonne
stations.lat_method: Méchain, repeating circle, at the École centrale, January-March 1797; Pole Star upper 200 observations 43 12 44.98, lower 234 observations 43 12 44.15; mean 434 observations 43 12 44.565; reduction to the tower of Saint-Vincent +9.742 (Méchain)
stations.azimuth_printed: Nore on the horizon of Saint-Vincent 201 18 58.9 (Vol. 2, p. 489); Vol. 3, p. 85 cites the observation as 201 18 58.0 against 201 19 36.9 calculated from Watten, excess +38.9
stations.source: Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, pp. 488-489, 641; Delambre & Méchain (1810), vol. 3, pp. 85, 89
stations.note: The table on Vol. 2, p. 642 prints Carcassonne 43 12 45.30; p. 641, p. 489 and Vol. 3, p. 89 print 43 12 54.30. Declination of the Pole Star supposed 88 13 27.00, mean for 1797 88 13 26.59.

stations.name: Perpignan
stations.lat_method: Méchain, one repeating circle, beta Ursae Minoris upper transit, 152 observations, 30 June to 16 July 1796; star place right ascension 14h 51m 27s and declination 74 59 19.65 for 1 January 1796; pendulum by Louis Berthoud set by Sun altitudes
stations.quote: Je n’ai pu retrouver ces observations du soleil, ni même les originaux des distances de l’étoile au zénith; j’ai seulement entre les mains trois copies des calculs de la latitude
stations.quote_en: I could not find these Sun observations, nor even the original zenith distances of the star; I have in hand only three copies of the latitude calculations
stations.note: Delambre had only three copies of Méchain's calculations, not the original zenith distances. The pages read do not state whether 42 42 3.32 refers to the observing place or to the tower of Saint-Jacques.

stations.name: Montjouy
stations.lat_method: Méchain, repeating circle divided in 360 degrees, December 1792 to January 1793; Pole Star upper 186 and lower 140 observations, total 326, 41 21 44.89; beta Ursae Minoris 41 21 45.21; alpha Draconis 41 21 45.07; mean 41 21 45.06, minus 0.1 to the tower. zeta Ursae Majoris not used (zenith distance 82 30 at lower transit)
stations.azimuth_printed: Matas observed 207 39 52.0 (Vol. 2, p. 138); calculated from Watten 207 40 15.4, excess +23.4
stations.source: Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, pp. 558, 641-642; Delambre & Méchain (1810), vol. 3, p. 85
stations.note: p. 641 prints the corrections as + 0.27 - 1.20. Pole Star declination supposed in 1793 88 12 9.00, corrected 88 12 8.86.

stations.name: Barcelona, Fontana de Oro
stations.lat_method: Méchain, repeating circle, 15 December 1793 to 1 January 1794; Pole Star upper 104 observations 41 22 47.00, lower 104 observations 41 22 47.87; difference of parallels to Montjouy -0 59.53
stations.deflection_printed: Reduced to Montjouy, Barcelona gives 41 21 47.90 by the Pole Star (+3.01 on Montjouy), 48.85 by beta Ursae Minoris (+3.64), 41 21 44.57 by zeta Ursae Majoris (+3.60); the two Barcelona circumpolar stars 41 21 48.37 against 41 21 45.06 at Montjouy, difference 3.21
stations.quote: Les trois étoiles circompolaires à Montjouy . . . 41° 21′ 45″06 Les deux de Barcelone . . . 41° 21′ 48″37 La différence est donc . . . 3″21
stations.quote_en: The three circumpolar stars at Montjouy: 41° 21′ 45.06″. The two at Barcelona: 41° 21′ 48.37″. The difference is therefore 3.21″

arcs.result_printed: degree 57082.63 toises at mean latitude 49 56 29.30; arc of one second 15.856283 toises
arcs.quote: L’arc entre Dunkerque et le Panthéon est de 124944.8, et la différence de latitude est 2° 11′ 19″83.
arcs.quote_en: The arc between Dunkerque and the Panthéon is 124944.8, and the difference of latitude is 2° 11′ 19.83″.

arcs.result_printed: degree 57069.31 toises at mean latitude 47 30 45.91; arc of one second 15.852586 toises
arcs.quote: L’arc entre le Panthéon et Évaux est de 152293.1 pour 2° 40′ 6″83. Le degré sera donc de 57069.31 à la latitude moyenne de 47° 30′ 45″91.
arcs.quote_en: The arc between the Panthéon and Évaux is 152293.1 for 2° 40′ 6.83″. The degree is therefore 57069.31 at the mean latitude 47° 30′ 45.91″.
arcs.note: Vol. 2, p. 642 prints the interval 2 40 6.92; Commission 2 40 5.44.

arcs.result_printed: degree 56977.80 toises at mean latitude 44 41 48.37; arc of one second 15.827167 toises
arcs.quote: L’arc entre Évaux et Carcassonne est de 168846.7, et l’arc céleste de 2° 57′ 48″24. Le degré sera donc de 56977.80 à la latitude moyenne de 44° 41′ 48″37.
arcs.quote_en: The arc between Évaux and Carcassonne is 168846.7, and the celestial arc 2° 57′ 48.24″. The degree is therefore 56977.80 at the mean latitude 44° 41′ 48.37″.
arcs.note: Vol. 2, p. 642 prints the interval 2 57 48.15; Commission 2 57 47.74.

arcs.result_printed: degree 56946.68 toises at mean latitude 42 17 19.60; arc of one second 15.818508 toises. With Barcelona's latitude (+3.24 on Montjouy) the arc becomes 1 51 6.1 and the degree 56974.31 (Vol. 3, p. 90)
arcs.quote: Enfin l’arc entre Carcassonne et Montjouy est de 105499, et l’arc céleste de 1° 51′ 9″34. Le degré sera donc de 56946.68 pour la latitude moyenne de 42° 17′ 19″6.
arcs.quote_en: Finally the arc between Carcassonne and Montjouy is 105499, and the celestial arc 1° 51′ 9.34″. The degree is therefore 56946.68 for the mean latitude 42° 17′ 19.6″.
arcs.note: Commission 1 51 9.58 (Vol. 2, p. 642). Decreases of the degree per degree of latitude printed in the table: 5.5, 32.4, 12.9.

arcs.result_printed: used for the flattening: second coefficient -83.5043 lignes in the metre formula
arcs.quote: On devoit être curieux de déterminer l’aplatissement par nos observations mêmes, et c’étoit dans cette vue que l’on avoit résolu d’observer la latitude à Évaux, qui tient à peu près le milieu entre Barcelone et Dunkerque.
arcs.quote_en: It was of interest to find the flattening from our own observations, and for this purpose it had been decided to observe the latitude at Évaux, which lies near the middle between Barcelona and Dunkerque.

arcs.note: Amplitude not printed on this page. From the latitudes on Vol. 3, p. 89 (51 2 9.20 minus 43 12 54.30) it is 7 49 14.90 (CALC).

arcs.length_printed: 551583.6385 toises (mean of two series); final 551584 toises; Commission 551584.72
arcs.result_printed: metre 443.2984 lignes; quarter meridian 5130776.85 toises against 5130740 adopted by the Commission (difference 36.85). Metre adopted 443.295936 lignes. Flattening best fitting the five latitudes: 1/150 (Laplace), 1/148 (Legendre), Vol. 3, p. 92
arcs.source: Delambre & Méchain (1810), vol. 3, pp. 77, 106-107; Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, p. 642
arcs.quote: Ainsi la petite diminution que, d’après des calculs plus exacts, j’ai faite à la base de Melun ... n’ont opéré qu’un changement également imperceptible dans la longueur de l’arc total qui définitivement sera de 551584 toises
arcs.quote_en: So the small decrease that I made to the Melun base after more exact calculation ... made only an equally imperceptible change in the length of the total arc, which will finally be 551584 toises
arcs.note: Metre table (Vol. 3, p. 106), arc entier: 1:150 443.2663; 1:200 443.3051; 1:250 443.3294; 1:300 443.3460; 1:310 443.3487; 1:320 443.3512; 1:330 443.3536; sphere 443.4341. With flattening 1/310 the mean of Barcelona and Montjouy gives 443.3280 against Dunkerque and 443.2658 against the Panthéon.

gaps: Longitudes: no astronomic longitude of any station was found on the pages read.
Évaux: the observer is not named on the pages read; the steeple latitude is printed three ways (42.444 p. 471, 42.45 p. 641, 42.54 p. 642 and Vol. 3).
Carcassonne: the table on Vol. 2, p. 642 prints 43 12 45.30; all other pages print 43 12 54.30. The intervals on p. 642 (2 40 6.92, 2 57 48.15) differ from Vol. 3, p. 89 (2 40 6.83, 2 57 48.24).
Dunkerque: Vol. 2, p. 640 prints the tower latitude once as 52° 2′ 9″2 (misprint for 51°).
Perpignan: the pages read do not say whether 42 42 3.32 is the observing place or the tower of Saint-Jacques; Delambre had no original zenith distances, only three copies of Méchain's calculations.
Barcelona: beta Ursae Minoris summary (Vol. 2, p. 612) read only in the text layer, not used for numbers. Barcelona is a separate point from Montjouy, connected by -0 59.53.
Azimuth raw registers for Bourges (Vol. 2, p. 131), Carcassonne (p. 135) and Montjouy (p. 138) not rendered; observed values taken from Vol. 3, pp. 84-85 and Vol. 2, p. 489.
Vol. 3, p. 92: Legendre's flattening for the latitude corrections is printed as 1/?20; the first digit of the denominator is not legible (3 or 5).
Vol. 3, p. 106: the 'Milieu' of the metre is printed 443.2?84 with the third decimal faint; p. 107 prints 443.2984.
Star catalogue: no named catalogue; declinations are those supposed and then corrected by Delambre (Vol. 2, pp. 632-639). The declination table on p. 632 was not rendered.
Montjouy register (Vol. 2, p. 503): the arc of the day for 20 December is partly illegible in the last digits; 15 December single arc last digit faint.
No grade-to-degree conversion is needed for Méchain's Montjouy and Barcelona registers (360-degree circle); Delambre's Dunkerque and Paris registers are in grades with a printed sexagesimal column.
